description: We are a motivated group of students passionate about space, science, technology, and innovation. We enjoy research, problem-solving, and building creative projects. We welcome people interested in AI/ML, Python, data analysis, web development, UI/UX, 3D visualization, and scientific research. Curiosity, creativity, and teamwork matter most to us.
summary:
FlameLens is an interactive, SI-powered dashboard developed to make NASA’s microgravity fire research easier to explore, understand, and use. It brings complex scientific findings into one accessible platform, helping users discover relevant experiments, compare research findings, and understand important insights about how flames behave in space. Instead of going through large volumes of technical reports, users can access summarized, ranked, and interpreted information in a much clearer way.

FlameLens addresses the Flame in Freefall challenge by transforming decades of NASA research into meaningful insights that can support fire-safety decisions for future space missions. This is especially important as astronauts prepare for longer journeys to the Moon and Mars, where even a small fire could become a serious threat. Our goal is to make valuable scientific knowledge more accessible and help contribute to safer human space exploration.
details:
FlameLens is an interactive, intelligence-powered research platform designed to make decades of NASA's microgravity combustion research easier to explore, compare, and understand. We developed it as a unified workspace where users can access NASA investigation records, explore experimental conditions, analyse available datasets, and discover insights relevant to fire safety in space.

The platform includes an Investigation Explorer, Comparison Lab, Model Lab, and an SI Research Copilot that answers research questions using indexed scientific evidence and provides source references for verification. It also features an interactive Storybook and Mission Deck to make complex combustion concepts easier to understand. Our analysis focuses on three major research areas: liquid-fuel flame extinction (FLEX), solid-fuel flame spread (BASS-II), and gas-phase jet combustion (SPICE).

What makes FlameLens different is its emphasis on scientific reliability. Instead of treating every experiment as directly comparable or presenting AI-generated predictions as facts, it considers experimental conditions, measurement definitions, units, data availability, and uncertainty before interpreting results. Its model workflows are designed to remain evidence-gated until sufficient data and validation are available.

We developed it as a software-based web application, deployed through Vercel, using NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) research records, local datasets, CSV/document processing, data analysis, and evidence-based retrieval. No specialised hardware is required.

Our creative approach combines scientific research, intelligent data exploration, interactive learning, and visual storytelling in one platform. Ultimately, we aim to help researchers make better use of existing knowledge, identify research gaps, and support more informed fire-safety research for future spacecraft, lunar habitats, and Mars missions.
